H4_refutation_detail.reason: Finite structured counterexamples were directionally separated by target rather than showing the preregistered cross-direction median pattern.
H4_refutation_detail.A: all 6 finite counterexamples started from current decision=false; none from true
H4_refutation_detail.B: all 12 finite counterexamples started from current decision=false; none from true

H4_refutation_detail.rule: No new operator is added to rescue the preregistered directional-asymmetry hypothesis.

main_findings: Logical same-G fragility and structured ecological-neighbourhood fragility are sharply different.

Most decisions identified in the original 64-world universe remained identified after expansion to the preregistered 2,592-world ecological lattice: 99.1 percent for A-release, 98.3 percent for B-release and 94.4 percent for M-release.
Under complete unrestricted same-G decomposition closure, only the 34 full-G truth cases remain trivially identified for each release target.
The resulting identifiability erosion ladder is 652 to 646 to 34 for A, 705 to 693 to 34 for B and 732 to 691 to 34 for M.
H4 was refuted rather than repaired: the finite ecological counterexamples were target- and direction-specific.
World-universe robustness must therefore report both the declared universe and the expansion operator family, not only a scalar identified/unidentified label.
claim_boundary: The structured lattice is a preregistered synthetic ecological neighbourhood, not an exhaustive or calibrated plausibility region.
No-counterexample within the lattice means robust to this frozen expansion only; it does not prove robustness to all biologically plausible worlds.
The complete same-G closure is a logical envelope and includes ecologically implausible states.
The 64-world, 2,592-world and complete-closure results are nested conditional certificates, not competing estimates of one probability.
The result does not alter the frozen BAM inverse-identifiability manuscript or EOG-WF empirical programme.
